source.anchor_kjv: I will declare thy name unto my brethren: in the midst of the congregation will I praise thee.
source.thread: Psalm 22 turns from the forsaken cry to praise in the congregation - Hebrews puts that verse in the mouth of the risen Christ, who is not ashamed to call us brethren
source.hook_line: Most people stop reading Psalm twenty-two at the cross.
source.spoken_script: Most people stop reading Psalm twenty-two at the cross. Keep going it doesn't end in a grave. But the cry doesn't stay forsaken. Later, the psalm turns the same voice moves from anguish to praise: "I will declare thy name unto my brethren: in the midst of the congregation will I praise thee." Who is that praising voice? Hebrews takes that opening line word for word and puts it in the mouth of the risen Christ. The psalm's turn is Jesus, alive on the far side of the cross. And hear what He calls us. Hebrews says He is "not ashamed to call them brethren" brothers. Family. The same Jesus who cried out forsaken now lives and the risen Christ is not ashamed to call His own brethren. He is calling you into that family.

platforms.label: YouTube (Long-form 16:9)
platforms.title: The Psalm That Turns: From Forsaken Cry to Family Song
platforms.description:
Psalm 22 opens with the cry Jesus prayed from the cross. But the psalm does not stay forsaken. Partway through, the same voice turns from anguish to praise (Psalm 22:22; Hebrews 2:11-12).

"I will declare thy name unto my brethren: in the midst of the congregation will I praise thee" (Psalm 22:22, KJV).

Who is the praising voice? The book of Hebrews answers: it places this verse in the mouth of the risen Christ, singing among his brethren. The turn in the psalm is Jesus, alive on the far side of the cross. And Hebrews adds the word that changes everything: he is not ashamed to call them brethren.

The One who cried forsaken now lives, and he is not ashamed to call his own family. He is calling you into that family.

redteam:
VERDICT: PASS

- KJV check: Psalm 22:22 is quoted verbatim as supplied, correctly attributed, front-loaded in YT/FB descriptions. The Hebrews 2:11 fragment "not ashamed to call them brethren" is verbatim. PASS.
- Citation honesty: the kit says Hebrews "puts this verse in the mouth of the risen Christ" and cites Hebrews 2:11-12 rather than claiming word-for-word identity (Hebrews 2:12 reads "church...sing praise", not "congregation...praise"). That precision is correct; do not tighten it into an identity claim in any future edit.
- instagram (minor, non-blocking): "Hebrews names the singer" is a hair looser than the text; Hebrews attributes the saying to Christ rather than naming a singer. Acceptable as compression, but "Hebrews says the speaker is the risen Jesus" would be tighter if the copy is ever revised.
- Titles: "Psalm 22 Does Not End at the Cross" is specific, honest, and does not collide with the sibling ps22 titles. No clickbait, no overclaim, no curiosity-gap lie.
- Platform fit: TikTok/Instagram lead with the hook in line one; tone appropriate per platform. Hashtags clean, no engagement-bait tags.
- Grace check: the landing ("calling you into that family") is invitation, no fear or gain-loss framing. PASS.
